stem: Fill in the blank: According to Le Chatelier’s principle, if a dynamic equilibrium is disturbed by changing the conditions, the position of equilibrium moves to ______ the change.
Fill in the blank: Le Chatelier’s principle can be used to predict the effect of a change in ______ on the position of equilibrium.
Fill in the blank: If a chemical system at equilibrium experiences a change in concentration, temperature, volume or partial pressure, then the equilibrium will shift to ______ the change.
Fill in the blank: In an exothermic reaction, an increase in temperature will shift the equilibrium to the ______ side.
Fill in the blank: According to Le Chatelier’s principle, an increase in pressure will favour the side of the reaction that has the ______ number of moles of gas.
True or false: The addition of a catalyst to a system at equilibrium changes the equilibrium position.
True or false: Decreasing the concentration of a product will shift the equilibrium to the right.
True or false: Le Chatelier’s principle can be applied to all types of reactions.
True or false: A decrease in temperature will shift the equilibrium to the side of an endothermic reaction.
True or false: An increase in volume will shift the reaction towards the side with more gas molecules.

Match the column. Column-I: (A) Le Chatelier’s principle (B) Increase in temperature in an exothermic reaction (C) Decrease in volume (D) Addition of catalyst (E) Increase in reactant concentration Column-II: (p) Shifts the equilibrium towards the reactants (q) Shifts the equilibrium towards the side with fewer gas molecules (r) Does not change the position of the equilibrium (s) The position of equilibrium moves to counteract the change (t) Shifts the equilibrium towards the products

key: (c) It counteracts the disturbance to attain a new equilibrium
stem: What does Le Chatelier’s principle state about a system at equilibrium when disturbed? (a) It stops reacting (b) It accelerates in the same direction (c) It counteracts the disturbance to attain a new equilibrium (d) It changes the equilibrium constant
Le Chatelier’s principle is not applicable to: (a) homogeneous reactions (b) heterogeneous reactions (c) homogeneous or heterogeneous systems in equilibrium (d) systems not in equilibrium

According to Le Chatelier’s principle, adding heat to a solid and liquid in equilibrium with endothermic nature will cause the (a) Temperature to rise (b) Temperature to fall (c) Amount of solid to decrease (d) Amount of liquid to decrease

On addition of an inert gas at constant volume to the reaction N 2 (g) + 3H 2 (g) ⇌ 2NH 3 (g) at equilibrium: (a) the reaction halts (b) forward reaction is favoured (c) the reaction remains unaffected (d) backward reaction is favoured

In a vessel containing SO 3 , SO 2 and O 2 at equilibrium, some helium gas is introduced so that the total pressure increases while temperature and volume remain constant. According to Le Chatelier’s principle the dissociation of SO 3 (a) increases (b) decreases (c) remains unaltered (d) changes unpredictably
Explain the effect of a catalyst on chemical equilibrium.
State and explain Le Chatelier’s principle suitably with reference to (1) change in temperature and (2) change in concentration.
What is the effect of adding chloride ion on the following equilibrium? AgCl(s) ⇌ Ag + (aq) + Cl − (aq)
For the equilibrium BaSO 4 (s) ⇌ Ba 2+ (aq) + SO 4 2− (aq), state the effect of: (a) Addition of Ba 2+ ion (b) Removal of SO 4 2− ion (c) Addition of BaSO 4 (s) on the equilibrium
What happens when more reactant is added to an equilibrium mixture? (a) Reaction shifts backward (b) Equilibrium constant decreases (c) Reaction shifts forward (d) No effect

When pressure is increased in a reaction where the product side has more gas moles than the reactant side, what happens? (a) Reaction moves forward (b) Reaction shifts backward (c) Equilibrium constant increases (d) Temperature rises

key: (c) Adding inert gas at constant volume
stem: Which of the following conditions causes no shift in the equilibrium position? (a) Changing temperature (b) Changing concentration (c) Adding inert gas at constant volume (d) Changing pressure
What effect does increasing temperature have on an endothermic reaction? (a) Shifts reaction backward (b) Has no effect (c) Shifts reaction forward (d) Decreases product concentration
For a reaction with more gaseous product moles than reactant moles, what happens when the pressure is doubled? (a) Shifts to product side (b) Shifts to reactant side (c) No effect (d) K increases
If pressure is reduced from 1 atm to 0.5 atm, by what factor does the concentration change? (a) Doubled (b) Halved (c) No change (d) Tripled
In a container, doubling the volume leads to what pressure change? (a) Doubles (b) Halves (c) Triples (d) No change
If an inert gas is added at constant volume, what is the effect on the equilibrium of N 2 + 3H 2 ⇌ 2NH 3 ? (a) Shifts forward (b) Shifts backward (c) No shift (d) K increases
In the equilibrium CaCO 3 (s) ⇌ CaO(s) + CO 2 (g), if volume is increased, what happens to the equilibrium? (a) Shifts to left (b) Shifts to right (c) No effect (d) Pressure decreases

In the reaction N 2 + 3H 2 ⇌ 2NH 3 , the initial pressure is 0.6 atm. The volume is decreased by half. How does the pressure change and what is the shift direction? (a) P = 1.2 atm, shift right (b) P = 1.2 atm, shift left (c) P = 0.3 atm, shift right (d) P = 0.3 atm, shift left
For the reaction A ⇌ B + C, if the initial moles of A are 1 mol in 1 L and K = 4, find the equilibrium moles of A after the reaction proceeds. (a) 0.5 mol (b) 0.33 mol (c) 0.25 mol (d) 0.2 mol

In PCl 5 ⇌ PCl 3 + Cl 2 , if the total pressure is increased from 1 atm to 2 atm, and the moles of products = 2 and reactant = 1, how does the concentration change and which direction is favoured? (a) Concentration doubles, backward shift (b) Concentration halves, forward shift (c) Concentration doubles, forward shift (d) No change

A container with CaCO 3 (s) ⇌ CaO(s) + CO 2 (g) has equilibrium at 1 atm. If the volume is increased, how do the pressure and direction change? (a) Pressure increases, forward (b) Pressure decreases, forward (c) Pressure decreases, backward (d) No effect
For an endothermic reaction, what is the effect of increasing the temperature followed by decreasing the volume? (a) Shift right, then left (b) Shift left, then right (c) Always right (d) No change

Consider the reaction CaCO 3 (s) ⇌ CaO(s) + CO 2 (g) in a closed container at equilibrium. What would be the effect of the addition of CaCO 3 on the equilibrium concentration of CO 2 ? (a) Increases (b) Unpredictable (c) Decreases (d) Remains unaffected

Consider the reaction PCl 5 (g) ⇌ PCl 3 (g) + Cl 2 (g) in a closed container at equilibrium. At a fixed temperature what will be the effect of adding more PCl 5 on the equilibrium concentration of Cl 2 (g)? (a) It decreases (b) It increases (c) It remains unaffected (d) It cannot be predicted without the value of K p

key: (b) an absorbent is used to remove SO₃ as soon as it is formed
stem: The equilibrium 2SO 2 (g) + O 2 (g) ⇌ 2SO 3 (g) shifts forward if: (a) a catalyst is used (b) an absorbent is used to remove SO 3 as soon as it is formed (c) small amounts of reactants are used (d) none of these
The equilibrium constants for the reaction Br 2 (g) ⇌ 2Br(g) at 500 K and 700 K are 1×10 −10 and 1×10 −5 respectively. The reaction is: (a) endothermic (b) exothermic (c) fast (d) slow
If pressure is applied to the following equilibrium, Liquid ⇌ Vapour, the boiling point of the liquid: (a) will decrease (b) will increase (c) may not change (d) will not change

In which equilibrium reaction would the equilibrium shift to the right if the total pressure is increased? (a) N 2 (g) + 3H 2 (g) ⇌ 2NH 3 (g) (b) H 2 (g) + I 2 (g) ⇌ 2HI(g) (c) H 2 (g) + Cl 2 (g) ⇌ 2HCl(g) (d) N 2 O 4 (g) ⇌ 2NO 2 (g)
Which equilibrium in the gaseous phase would be unaffected by an increase in pressure? (a) N 2 O 4 ⇌ 2NO 2 (b) N 2 + O 2 ⇌ 2NO (c) N 2 + 3H 2 ⇌ 2NH 3 (d) CO + ½O 2 ⇌ CO 2

For the chemical reaction 3X(g) + Y(g) → X 3 Y(g), the amount of X 3 Y at equilibrium is affected by: (a) temperature and pressure (b) temperature only (c) pressure only (d) temperature, pressure and catalyst

In a flask, colourless N 2 O 4 is in equilibrium with brown-coloured NO 2 . At equilibrium, when the flask is heated at 100 °C the brown colour deepens, and on cooling it becomes less coloured. The change in enthalpy ΔH for the system is: (a) negative (b) positive (c) zero (d) undefined

The exothermic formation of ClF 3 is represented by the equation Cl 2 (g) + 3F 2 (g) ⇌ 2ClF 3 (g); ΔH = −329 kJ. Which of the following will increase the quantity of ClF 3 in an equilibrium mixture of Cl 2 , F 2 and ClF 3 ? (a) Increasing the temperature (b) Removing Cl 2 (c) Increasing the volume of the container (d) Adding F 2 📝 PYQ: AIEEE 2005 Solution ↗

An increase in the temperature of an equilibrium system: (a) favours the exothermic reaction (b) favours the endothermic reaction (c) favours both the exothermic and endothermic reactions (d) favours neither the exothermic nor the endothermic reaction

key: (c) a new reaction pathway to reaction
stem: A chemical system is in equilibrium. Addition of a catalyst would result in: (a) increase in the rate of forward reaction (b) increase in the rate of reverse reaction (c) a new reaction pathway to reaction (d) increase in the amount of heat evolved in the reaction

In which of the following reactions does an increase in pressure at constant temperature not affect the moles at equilibrium? (a) 2NH 3 (g) ⇌ N 2 (g) + 3H 2 (g) (b) C(g) + ½O 2 (g) ⇌ CO 2 (g) (c) H 2 (g) + ½O 2 (g) ⇌ H 2 O(g) (d) H 2 (g) + I 2 (g) ⇌ 2HI(g)

In which of the following equilibria does a change in volume of the system not alter the number of moles? (a) N 2 (g) + O 2 (g) ⇌ 2NO(g) (b) PCl 5 (g) ⇌ PCl 3 (g) + Cl 2 (g) (c) N 2 (g) + 3H 2 (g) ⇌ 2NH 3 (g) (d) SOCl 2 (g) ⇌ SO 2 (g) + Cl 2 (g) 📝 PYQ: AIEEE 2002 Solution ↗

key: (a) lowering the temperature and increasing pressure
stem: Predict the condition for the forward reaction on the basis of Le Chatelier’s principle for 2SO 2 (g) + O 2 (g) ⇌ 2SO 3 (g); ΔH = −198 kJ. (a) lowering the temperature and increasing pressure (b) any value of temperature and pressure (c) lowering of temperature as well as pressure (d) increasing temperature as well as pressure 📝 PYQ: AIEEE 2003 Solution ↗

The equilibrium constant for the reaction N 2 (g) + O 2 (g) ⇌ 2NO(g) is 4×10 −4 at 2000 K. In the presence of a catalyst the equilibrium is attained ten times faster. Therefore the equilibrium constant, in the presence of the catalyst, at 2000 K is: (a) 40×10 −4 (b) 4×10 −4 (c) 4×10 −3 (d) difficult to compute without more data

The graph relates ln K eq against 1/T for a reaction, and the plotted straight line has a positive slope. The reaction must be: (a) exothermic (b) endothermic (c) ΔH is negligible (d) highly spontaneous at ordinary temperature

[One or more than one option may be correct] Consider the reactions given below. In which cases will the reaction proceed toward the right by increasing the pressure? (a) 4HCl(g) + O 2 (g) → 2Cl 2 (g) + 2H 2 O(g) (b) Cl 2 (g) + H 2 O(g) → 2HCl(g) + ½O 2 (g) (c) CO 2 (g) + 4H 2 (g) → CH 4 (g) + 2H 2 O(g) (d) N 2 (g) + O 2 (g) → 2NO(g)

key: (c), (d) inert gas at constant pressure; increasing the volume
stem: [One or more than one option may be correct] For the reaction PCl 5 (g) ⇌ PCl 3 (g) + Cl 2 (g), the forward reaction at constant temperature is favoured by: (a) introducing an inert gas at constant volume (b) introducing chlorine gas at constant volume (c) introducing an inert gas at constant pressure (d) increasing the volume of the container

key: (c) The reaction is retarded by the addition of hydrogen ion
stem: [One or more than one option may be correct] Indicate the correct answer out of the following for the reaction NH 4 Cl + H 2 O ⇌ NH 4 OH + HCl (a) The reaction is retarded by the addition of KOH (b) The reaction is favoured by the addition of NH 4 OH (c) The reaction is retarded by the addition of hydrogen ion (d) None of these

key: (c) increasing temperature favours the forward reaction
stem: When NaNO 3 is heated in a closed vessel, oxygen is liberated and NaNO 2 is left behind. At equilibrium (a) addition of NaNO 2 favours the reverse reaction (b) addition of NaNO 2 favours the forward reaction (c) increasing temperature favours the forward reaction (d) decreasing pressure favours the reverse reaction

key: (b) low temperature, high pressure and catalyst
stem: Favourable conditions for the manufacture of ammonia by the reaction N 2 (g) + 3H 2 (g) ⇌ 2NH 3 (g); ΔH = −21.9 kcal are: (a) low temperature, low pressure and catalyst (b) low temperature, high pressure and catalyst (c) high temperature, low pressure and catalyst (d) high temperature, high pressure and catalyst

key: (d) the rate of formation of ammonia would be too slow
stem: The Haber’s process for the manufacture of ammonia is usually carried out at about 500 °C. If a temperature of about 250 °C was used instead of 500 °C: (a) ammonia would not be formed at all (b) the percentage of ammonia in the equilibrium mixture would be too low (c) a catalyst would be of no use at all at this temperature (d) the rate of formation of ammonia would be too slow

Passage (Q4–Q5). If a system at equilibrium is subjected to a change in concentration, pressure or temperature, the system adjusts itself so as to minimise the effect of that change. For solubility: when solid substances dissolve in water heat may be evolved or absorbed; for an endothermic dissolution the solubility increases with temperature and for an exothermic dissolution it decreases. When a gas dissolves in a liquid there is a decrease in volume, so an increase of pressure favours dissolution. A gaseous solute ‘X’ when dissolved in water evolves heat. Then the solubility of ‘X’ will increase at: (a) High temperature, low pressure (b) Low temperature, high pressure (c) High temperature, high pressure (d) Low temperature, low pressure

key: (b) Concentration of all the components at equilibrium will change
stem: Passage (Q4–Q5), continued. For the reaction N 2 (g) + O 2 (g) ⇌ 2NO(g), if the pressure is increased by reducing the volume of the container then: (a) Total pressure at equilibrium will remain the same (b) Concentration of all the components at equilibrium will change (c) Concentration of all the components at equilibrium will remain the same (d) Equilibrium will shift in the backward direction

Passage (Q6–Q9). The variation of the equilibrium constant K with temperature is given by the van’t Hoff equation ln K = ΔS r °/R − ΔH r °/RT, from which ΔH r ° can be evaluated if the equilibrium constants K 1 and K 2 at two temperatures T 1 and T 2 are known: log(K 2 /K 1 ) = (ΔH r °/2.303R)[1/T 1 − 1/T 2 ]. For an isomerization X(g) ⇌ Y(g), the temperature dependency of the equilibrium constant is given by ln K = 2 − 1000/T. The value of Δ r S° at 300 K is: (a) 2R (b) 2/R (c) 1000R (d) None of these

key: (b) For an exothermic reaction K eq increases with decreasing temperature
stem: Passage (Q6–Q9), continued. Select the correct statement: (a) The value of K eq always increases with increasing temperature (b) For an exothermic reaction the value of K eq increases with decreasing temperature (c) For an endothermic reaction the value of K eq increases with decreasing temperature (d) For an exothermic reaction the slope of log K vs 1/T is negative

Passage (Q6–Q9), continued. The variation of log 10 K with 1/T is shown by a graph in which the straight line rises at 45°. Hence ΔH° is: (a) −4.606 kJ/mol (b) −19.147 kJ/mol (c) 8.314 kJ/mol (d) 10 kJ/mol

Passage (Q6–Q9), continued. The equilibrium constant K p for the reaction A(g) ⇌ B(g) + C(g) is 1 at 27 °C and 4 at 47 °C. For the reaction B(g) + C(g) ⇌ A(g), calculate the enthalpy change. (Given: R = 2 cal/mol·K) (a) −13.31 kcal/mol (b) 13.31 kcal/mol (c) −19.2 kcal/mol (d) 55.63 kcal/mol

key: (a), (b), (c) all three concentrations fall; moles of NH₃ fall; the cooling depends on the amount of He
stem: [Multiple correct] N 2 (g) and H 2 (g) are allowed to react in a closed vessel at a given temperature and pressure for the formation of NH 3 (g) [N 2 (g) + 3H 2 (g) ⇌ 2NH 3 (g) + 22.4 kcal]. If He(g) is added at equilibrium at constant pressure , then which is/are correct? (a) Concentration of N 2 (g), H 2 (g) and NH 3 (g) decrease (b) Moles of NH 3 (g) decreases (c) The extent of cooling depends on the amount of He(g) added (d) Concentration of N 2 and H 2 increases and concentration of NH 3 decreases
